```text
# #4246: Patch: screen the reply's switched-off combined lethal again and switch it on if the screen keeps it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the computer opponent imagines your next turn, it currently scores its attacks one hit at a time. So it can misevaluate a board where two attackers only win the game together: it sees a mere kill, spends an attacker removing a unit, and misses that sending both at your hero would end the game. Since the newest change it can also do the reverse: hide a unit in Defense and watch its own imagined combined lethal evaporate. A built-in alternative already exists that counts all remaining attacks together and sends them at the hero first when they reach past the blockers. It is switched off because a single measurement on 2026-11-01 came out flat (203-197 on 400 games, edge +0.015 with an interval crossing zero). This re-runs that measurement on today's opponent model and flips the switch only if the new measurement says the alternative plays better. Players notice slightly sharper computer attacks and blocks; nothing else changes.

## Why

- The design already invites this: SPEC 9.9's opponent's-reply paragraph describes the combined-lethal reply and says it is switched off (`AI_REPLY.open_lethal`) until a screen keeps it.
- The 2026-11-01 screen predates five changes to the reply: combined damage-pool and conversion reads (R4064000/R4064001), Burn/Toxic and exile blow pricing (R4065000/R4065001), per-attack combat math with First-Strike-stopped blows worth nothing (R4171000), and the new Defense-switch wall logic (R4187000). The old reading measured a different reply.
- R4187000's own ruling note documents a concrete mis-evaluation under the current setting: with the switch off, the reply's attack is one hit, a wall beats it on the evaluation's flat lethal-threat cliff, and with two 4/4s against the seat at 8 the opponent walls and misses its own combined lethal. The switch is exactly the guard that case wants: with it on, attacks that together reach the hero count as the win, so the attack wins the comparison and the lethal is taken.
- Nothing open or recently closed covers this: #1283 (lethal against every trap) is the solver's hidden-card coverage, a different mechanism, and #3823 (ranking the AI's own prompt answers) stays untouched.

## Proposal

1. Build a candidate with `open_lethal: true` and nothing else changed.
2. Predeclare the screen size (400 improve-dev games is the floor; 800 if the expected gain is a point or two), then run the arena screen from training/improve.md (`arena --set improve-dev`, candidate as self against a control built from the committed tip). Trace losses with `cargo jackioh trace`. Never screen on gate deals, which stay hold-out.
3. Keep the flip only if the paired edge's low end is above zero; otherwise revert and record the numbers on the issue. No extending a close screen and no second run for a better read, per the screen rules.
4. The existing `open_lethal_1634` tests already thread both settings through `simulate_reply_with` and assert the shipped behavior follows the constant, so the flip is test-held by construction; add a `run_puzzle` case in that module only if a trace finds a new concrete position.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (`AI_REPLY.open_lethal` and its screen comment)
- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (no change expected; `simulate_reply_with` already threads the flag)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs` (`open_lethal_1634` module, only if a trace finds a new puzzle)
- `spec/09-architecture.md`, 9.9 opponent's-reply paragraph (the until-a-screen-keeps-it sentence, updated to the outcome)
- Procedure followed: `training/improve.md`, A screen

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Screen size predeclared on the issue before it starts; control built from the committed tip.
- [ ] Arena tally reported with wins and paired edge plus 95 percent interval; kept only if the low end is above zero, else reverted with numbers recorded.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` green and `cargo jackioh spec check` green.
- [ ] No gate-deal seeds used in any screen.
- [ ] The spec sentence matches the shipped value.

## Size and risks

Small code change (one constant, its comment, one spec sentence), hard measurement: 400-800 arena games of compute, roughly an hour on a runner. Difficulty is hard by the AI convention. The main risk is the appearance of re-rolling one switch until it turns green; it is contained by the changed conditions (five reply changes plus a newly documented bad interaction), a predeclared size, and keep-only-above-zero with no extensions. If the retire-the-learned-evaluation proposal lands first this is unaffected (reply ranking, not evaluation). No hidden-information change: the flag only re-ranks attacks on the same sampled worlds.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44656595228)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Flip the AI's combined-lethal reply switch (`AI_REPLY.open_lethal`) from `false` to `true` if and only if a predeclared arena screen on the fixed dev set (`improve-dev`) keeps it: candidate as self against a control built from the committed tip, kept only when the paired edge's low end is above zero, otherwise reverted with the numbers recorded on the issue. Update the §9.9 spec sentence to match the shipped value. No other behavior changes.

## Files to touch

| File | New or change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/ai/src/config.rs` | change | `AI_REPLY.open_lethal`: `false` to `true`, and its screen comment rewritten with the new screen's numbers |
| `spec/09-architecture.md` | change | §9.9 opponent's-reply paragraph: the "switched off (`AI_REPLY.open_lethal`) until a screen keeps it" sentence, updated to the outcome |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs` | change only if a trace finds a new puzzle | a new `run_puzzle` case in the existing `open_lethal_1634` module |
| `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` | no change expected | `simulate_reply_with` already threads the flag; reference only |

Must not touch: anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/`; `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, or any test outside `crates/ai`; gate seeds, seed sets, or thresholds; `docs/polish/3-ai.md` (its "switched off until a screen keeps it" line is out of this issue's scope, see Risks); `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/CARDS.md`. No new ruling note: no spec-undecided rules question is being settled (the combined-lethal read is #1634's mechanism plus R4187000's guard), so no free R-number is consumed. Governing spec: §9.9 opponent's-reply paragraph; governing rulings: R4187000 (the wall-vs-attack comparison this switch guards), R4064000/R4064001, R4171000 (the five reply changes since the 2026-11-01 screen).

## Steps

1. Read the touch points before changing anything: `AI_REPLY` and its `open_lethal` doc comment in `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (around lines 993-1026), `simulate_reply` / `simulate_reply_with` and the `face_is_lethal = open_lethal && ready_gap(...) <= 0.0` line in `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (lines 724-809), `ready_gap` in `crates/ai/src/lethal.rs` (line 174), the `open_lethal_1634` module in `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs` (lines 743-802), the §9.9 paragraph in `spec/09-architecture.md`, and the "A screen" section of `training/improve.md`.
2. Predeclare the screen on the issue before running it: post a comment naming the size (400 games is the floor; use `--games 800` if the expected gain is a point or two) and that the control is built from the committed tip. Never screen on gate deals; the arena refuses them.
3. Build the control from the committed tip with no changes applied: `cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools && cp target/release/jackioh ~/control-jackioh`.
4. Make the candidate: the one-line change `open_lethal: false` to `open_lethal: true` in `AI_REPLY` in `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, nothing else. Then run the screen: `cargo jackioh arena --a self --b bin:~/control-jackioh --set improve-dev` (add `--games 800` only if that is what step 2 predeclared). Record the closing tally: wins, `aShare` with its interval, `deals`, and the paired `edge` with `edgeLow` to `edgeHigh`.
5. Trace the candidate's losses with `cargo jackioh trace` (dev-set games only, never the gate's) to check for a new concrete mis-evaluation position worth a regression test.
6. Keep the flip only if `edgeLow` is above zero; otherwise revert the constant to `false` exactly and record the full tally on the issue. No extending a close screen and no second run for a better read.
7. If kept: rewrite the `open_lethal` comment in `crates/ai/src/config.rs` following the pattern of the neighboring `defense_switches` comment (issue number, games, wins, edge with interval, the lane reference), and update the §9.9 sentence in `spec/09-architecture.md` so it states the shipped value (on, kept by the new screen) instead of "switched off until a screen keeps it".
8. If step 5 found a new concrete position, add one `run_puzzle` case to the `open_lethal_1634` module in `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`, copying the shape of `decide_blocks_one_of_two_attackers_that_are_lethal_only_together` (setup JSON, `run_puzzle`, `all_out_attack`, `trace` in the assertion message). The existing tests already assert `simulate_reply` follows `AI_REPLY.open_lethal`, so no other test edit is needed.

## Tests

- `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`, `open_lethal_1634` module (existing, must keep passing; they pin both settings and the shipped switch): `b41_takes_a_lethal_that_needs_both_attacks_over_a_kill_worth_more_than_one_hit`, `decide_blocks_one_of_two_attackers_that_are_lethal_only_together`. Command: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai reply`.
- Any new `run_puzzle` case added in step 8, by its exact new test name, asserting the post-flip behavior (both attackers sent at the hero; e.g. game won by the reply where the old setting killed a unit instead). Command: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai <new test name>`.
- Full crate suite: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` (engine rule tests are untouched, but run the AI crate green). Lints and spec: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Screen size was predeclared on the issue before it ran; control was built from the committed tip.
- [ ] Arena tally reported with wins and paired edge plus 95 percent interval; flip kept only with low end above zero, else reverted with numbers recorded on the issue.
- [ ] No gate-deal seeds used in any screen; no extended or repeated screen.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` green; `cargo jackioh spec check` green; fmt and clippy clean.
- [ ] The §9.9 sentence matches the shipped `open_lethal` value.

## Risks

- Re-rolling one switch until it turns green: contained by changed conditions (five reply changes plus R4187000 since the 2026-11-01 screen), a predeclared size, and keep-only-above-zero with no extensions. Mitigation is procedural: do steps 2-6 in order and record everything on the issue.
- The arena costs roughly an hour of compute (400-800 games); start it only when it can finish in the run's budget, per the lane's own rule.
- `docs/polish/3-ai.md` still says the switch is "off until a screen keeps it" and goes stale if the flip is kept; the issue's Where-it-lands scopes it out, so leave it and name it in the pull request notes rather than expanding this change.
- Hidden-information safety is unchanged: the flag only re-ranks attacks on the same sampled worlds (`face_is_lethal` from `ready_gap` on the determinized state).

## Open questions

None. The only judgment call the task leaves open (screen size within the 400/800 bounds) is settled by the builder's predeclared choice on the issue.
```
